questions.prompt: What should the report contain if a product keeps its ID and values but moves to a different position and is represented by a new object?
questions.evidence: After requesting and receiving the full explanation, the candidate explicitly requested moving on instead of providing their own prediction.

questions.prompt: With n previous and m current products, what are the time and auxiliary-space costs of your implementation, and which operation-cost assumptions support those bounds?
questions.evidence: Identified quadratic cross-list work as O(n*m), but conflated constant-time hash lookup with total algorithm time and explicitly requested an explanation of auxiliary memory.

questions.prompt: In your implementation, where would a Set of IDs be sufficient, and where would access to the corresponding product record still be necessary?
questions.evidence: Correctly identified addition and removal detection as membership-only checks; did not explicitly discuss record access for field comparison.

stages.title: Core Task
stages.skipReason: Candidate explicitly stopped the unfinished Core and requested review of the existing code.

observations: Six focused behavior checks passed, including empty sides, ID replacement, value equality, and name/price changes, with frozen inputs.
Changed records follow previous order rather than the required current order; a reversed two-product case failed.
Both traversals perform full-array find calls, retaining O(n*m+n+m) worst-case work instead of the expected linear target.

knowledgeSignals.evidence: Correctly identified addition/removal detection as ID membership checks and implemented baseline matching by ID.
Recognized O(n*m) work but required explanation to distinguish lookup cost from total cost and to analyze auxiliary/output memory.
Changed results use previous traversal order; the current-order acceptance check fails.
Focused checks run successfully with frozen source arrays and records; outputs retain source references without mutating inputs.

mastery.label: Partially working
mastery.reason: Podstawowa klasyfikacja produktów działa, ale dwa istotne wymagania — kolejność zmian i liniowe porównanie list — pozostają niespełnione; samodzielna analiza pamięci oraz przełożenie indeksowania na kod wymagają dalszej praktyki.

topicSignals.evidence: Baseline ID matching works and the candidate identified membership-only checks, but could not implement indexed lookup to meet the core linear-time target.
Recognized cross-list O(n*m) work; confused one hash lookup with total algorithm cost and required an explanation of auxiliary and output memory.
Changed results still use unshift during previous traversal after explanation and step-by-step guidance; the same-order two-change check fails.
Current flat-record comparison preserves frozen source arrays and products and reuses references safely; this does not establish mastery of nested immutable updates.
